hypotheses.summary: H1 (identity→storage, cache poisoning): SUPPORTED. canRead caches decisions in store.readDecisions keyed ONLY by projectId (policy.mjs:6-12), so the first requester's decision is reused for every other user of the same project; also never invalidated on revocation.

H2 (HTTP→jobs, cross-project document binding): createExport validates membership only in body.projectId, but never checks that body.documentId belongs to that project. An orchard member can queue an export with projectId='orchard' and documentId='doc-harbor' (or any other project's doc); worker then renders doc-harbor and downloadExport (owner check only) discloses it. Also no check that documentId exists at creation time.

H3 (jobs→storage→HTTP, revocation bypass): worker sets job.result using job.documentId with no membership re-check, and downloadExport checks only job.userId, never current membership. After revocation, a queued (or already-ready) job still discloses the former project's document. README explicitly requires revocation to invalidate queued exports, so this is a stated security requirement violation.

H4 (HTTP input validation): REJECTED as a security issue. body.projectId missing a type check fails closed (nonexistent project → 'forbidden' in requireFreshMembership); Maps prevent prototype pollution; requireSession handles absent sessions. Only minor robustness nit: body.projectId lacks a string type check, symmetric with documentId, but no exploitable path found.

entry.title: High (H-3): Queued/ready export jobs bypass membership revocation — job result is a perpetual disclosure grant
entry.summary: Medium/High: A queued export job is a perpetual grant. runExportWorker (packages/jobs/worker.mjs:2-8) executes queued jobs with no membership re-check at execution time, and downloadExport (packages/http/api.mjs:23-28) checks only job.userId and state==='ready', never current membership. After a user's membership in the project is revoked, both a still-queued job (processed post-revocation) and an already-ready job's stored result remain downloadable, disclosing the former project's document. README explicitly states 'A queued job is work to validate, not a perpetual grant' and 'Membership revocation must ... prevent queued exports from disclosing the former project's documents' — the implementation does not satisfy either. Source→sink: job{userId,projectId,documentId} persisted at creation → worker copies doc.body into job.result unconditionally → download returns job.result after only an ownership check. Note: no revocation/membership-mutation API exists in the repo, so this is latent until revocation is implemented; severity reflects the stated requirement.
entry.impact: Former members retain permanent read access to project documents through exports they created while a member, violating the service's stated security requirement (README lines 13-15).
entry.exploitPreconditions: Job queued while user was a member; membership later revoked; worker runs (for queued jobs) or job already ready; user downloads own job.

entry.title: Critical (C-1): readDecisions authorization cache ignores user identity — cross-user access control bypass
entry.summary: Critical: Authorization decision cache keyed per-project only — cross-user decision reuse and revocation failure. canRead() (packages/identity/policy.mjs:6-12) caches the boolean result in store.readDecisions.get(projectId) without including userId in the key. The first caller for a project fixes the answer for ALL users: if alice (orchard member) reads any orchard doc first, bob (harbor-only) is then granted 'orchard quarterly results' via readDocument (packages/http/api.mjs:5-12). Conversely a non-member's denial poisons members. Source→sink: session userId (trusted gateway) → requireSession → canRead(userId, projectId) → readDecisions.get(projectId) reuses other user's cached boolean → doc.body returned. No invalidation/TTL exists anywhere in the repo (store.mjs:13 initializes the cache; nothing removes entries).
entry.impact: Complete cross-user authorization bypass on document reads. If the first reader of project P is a member, every non-member gains read access to all of P's documents indefinitely; if the first reader is a non-member, all members are denied (DoS). Cache is also never invalidated, so even per-user revocation would not take effect on cached grants.
entry.exploitPreconditions: Two different users share the store instance (stated in README: one shared store); any project that has been queried once by any user. Read access via readDocument (GET /documents/:id).

entry.title: High (H-2): Export creation does not bind documentId to the authorized projectId — cross-project document exfiltration via exports
entry.summary: High: createExport (packages/http/api.mjs:14-21) authorizes membership for body.projectId but queues body.documentId without ever verifying the document exists or belongs to that project. A member of 'orchard' can POST /exports {projectId:'orchard', documentId:'doc-harbor'}; runExportWorker (packages/jobs/worker.mjs:2-8) then reads store.documents.get('doc-harbor') with no authorization check and stores harbor's document body in job.result; downloadExport (api.mjs:23-28) checks only job.userId===creator and returns the harbor content. Source→transform→sink: client-controlled body.documentId → requireFreshMembership(body.projectId) mismatch → job persisted → worker reads arbitrary doc → CSV result → returned to creator. Counterevidence checked: no other handler or worker path re-validates document project ownership (all four handlers and worker read in full).
entry.impact: Any authenticated member of any project can exfiltrate every other project's documents through the export pipeline, bypassing membership entirely. No authorization check ever sees the document's real project.
entry.exploitPreconditions: Authenticated member of any project A; knowledge or guess of another project's document id (ids are simple slugs like 'doc-harbor'); worker must run before download.
